subject: Azure private plan — Novorx negotiated terms & IP/data residency
messages:
From: Rick Patel <procurement@novorx.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Susan Owens <susan.owens@azuremarketplace.microsoft.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T18:12:00Z
Subject: Azure private plan — initial commercial asks

Michael,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Novorx is ready to move forward with an Azure private plan but we need to lock a few commercial/legal items before procurement will sign: 

- Data residency: Novorx requires EU-only processing for customer PII tied to EU customers; can Redwood commit to a European-only tenant for our private plan?
- IP & license carve-outs: our external counsel has requested a clause clarifying that Novorx retains ownership of customer prompts and derived business outputs.
- Entitlements & metering: confirm how entitlements map to Azure SKUs and whether we can split billing to our centralized procurement (they require a seller-provided invoice).

I've attached our internal term sheet for reference. Can we get a redline back this week? If you prefer, loop in your legal team and we can do a short review call.

Thanks,
Rick Patel
Head of Procurement | Novorx
procurement@novorx.com
Attachment: Novorx_Azure_PrivatePlan_Termsheet_20260302.pdf (application/pdf, 98 KB)

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Rick Patel <procurement@novorx.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T21:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Azure private plan — initial commercial asks

Thanks Rick — appreciate the clear list. Looping in Lauren (partner/marketplace) to confirm co-sell/metering semantics, and copying Neha (legal) to start the DPA/IP questions.

Quick notes from our side:
- EU tenant: We can provision an EU-only deployment for the private plan; we'll need to capture the expected region pairs and residency SLA in the SOW.
- IP: Redwood's standard terms preserve customer content ownership; I'll ask Neha to propose explicit language for prompts/derived outputs so your counsel can review.
- Billing/entitlements: Azure private SKUs require mapping from our entitlements to an Azure Private Offer; Lauren will clarify whether we can emit a seller invoice or if invoicing must flow through Marketplace commerce.

I'll get an initial redline from legal by EOD Friday and propose a 30-minute alignment call early next week.

Cheers,
Michael Grant
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
+1 415-555-0139
Attachment: None

From: Rick Patel <procurement@novorx.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: external-counsel@novorx.com, Susan Owens <susan.owens@azuremarketplace.microsoft.com>
Date: 2026-03-04T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Azure private plan — Novorx negotiated terms & IP/data residency

Michael — appreciate the quick turnaround. Attached is our counsel's redline (PDF) with the requested IP language and a proposed data residency exhibit. Highlights: 

- Section 4.2 (Data Processing): require explicit wording that Novorx customer PII is processed and stored only in EU data centers for EU customers; include subprocessor list and monthly attestation.
- New clause on outputs: "Customer Outputs and Prompt Data are the exclusive property of Customer; Supplier (Redwood) will not assert any rights."
- Indemnity: limited carve-outs for gross negligence; we propose a mutual cap at 12 months of fees.

Can Neha review and call out which items are deal blockers versus language that can be accepted for procurement?

Thanks — attaching Novorx_Azure_PrivatePlan_Redlines_v3.pdf

Rick
Attachment: Novorx_Azure_PrivatePlan_Redlines_v3.pdf (application/pdf, 212 KB)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Rick Patel <procurement@novorx.com>, external-counsel@novorx.com
Date: 2026-03-05T14:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Azure private plan — review of Novorx redlines

Team — I reviewed Novorx's redlines and flagged the following items: 

1) Data residency / subprocessor clause: We can commit to EU-only processing for EU customer data if Novorx accepts the standard subprocessor notification cadence (30 days) and an SLA addendum; we should avoid a monthly attestation requirement (operationally heavy). Propose: "Supplier will maintain EU-only processing for EU Customer Data and will provide annual attestation and 30-day notification of material subprocessor changes."

2) Ownership of prompts/outputs: Redwood is comfortable with explicit language confirming Customer ownership of prompts and business outputs. We should add a reciprocal right: Redwood may use aggregated, deidentified telemetry for product improvement; exclude fine-tuning on raw customer prompts unless separately contracted.

3) Indemnity/cap: Mutual cap at 12 months of fees is acceptable for commercial accounts; however, for enterprise data-sensitive customers we normally take a higher cap. Recommend settling on 12 months for this private plan and note exceptions for willful misconduct.

4) Billing / seller invoice: Lauren, can you confirm whether Azure will allow us to issue a seller invoice to Novorx rather than routing through Marketplace? If not, we should propose an AM/PM (account manager / procurement) workflow that attaches invoicing artifacts to the marketplace purchase.

Next steps I propose:
- Michael/ Lauren: confirm invoicing path by EOD 3/6
- I will produce a redline of Novorx's PDF with the proposed language (target 3/6 EOD)
- 30-minute call Wednesday 3/8 to review final terms before DocuSign

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Attachment: None

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Rick Patel <procurement@novorx.com>, Susan Owens <susan.owens@azuremarketplace.microsoft.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-06T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Azure private plan — Novorx negotiated terms & IP/data residency

Thanks everyone — good alignment. Quick summary/asks: 

- Redwood will deliver a PDF redline with: (a) EU-only processing + annual attestation & 30-day subprocessor notice, (b) explicit customer ownership of prompts/outputs + deidentified telemetry carve-out, (c) mutual cap at 12 months fees with standard exceptions. Neha will upload the redline to the HubSpot deal record.
- Lauren confirms: Azure will accept a seller-provided invoice for this Private Offer (confirmed offline with MS contact). We will emit seller invoices to Novorx; however initial onboarding invoice may flow through Marketplace commerce for entitlement activation. Lauren will send a short note on the invoicing timeline.
- Proposed next step: Neha to send final redline (PDF) and I will send DocuSign link for signature after Novorx confirmation. Target: signature by 3/12.

Rick — can you confirm Novorx counsel is okay with the annual attestation in lieu of monthly attestation and the mutual cap? If yes, I'll push the signed DocuSign envelope and route invoices per Lauren's note.

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
Attachment: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-98765 (HubSpot deal), DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/ABCDEF1234567890
